extractor_notes: Denied classes are enumerated in section 'B. Classes Considered but Not Recommended' (Final Rule pp. 17-18). Section B lists 4 numbered discussions covering 5 proposed class numbers (Classes 8 and 10 are treated jointly). The preamble (p. 3) also notes that 3 of the 44 petitions filed in response to the NOI 'sought exemptions that could not be granted as a matter of law' and were not put forward for public comment in the NPRM; those 3 are not enumerated by topic in the Final Rule and were never assigned a Proposed Class number, so they are not listed below. NPRM grouped the remaining petitions into 27 proposed classes; the 10 granted classes account for 22 proposed-class numbers (Classes 1-7 audiovisual; 9 accessibility; 11-15 wireless unlocking; 16-17 smartphone/tablet jailbreaking; 20 smart-TV jailbreaking; 21 vehicles; 22+25+27A security research; 23 abandoned video games; 26 3D printers; 27B medical devices), leaving Classes 8, 10, 18, 19, 24 as the denied set, which matches the Final Rule's Section B exactly.
